[[File:Definition-of-a-nodal-decomposition.jpg|thumb|Nodal decomposition.]] In [[category theory]], an abstract mathematical discipline, a '''nodal decomposition'''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=28}} of a morphism <math>\varphi:X\to Y</math> is a representation of <math>\varphi</math> as a product <math>\varphi=\sigma\circ\beta\circ\pi</math>, where <math>\pi</math> is a [[Epimorphism#Related concepts|strong epimorphism]],<ref>An [[epimorphism]] <math>\varepsilon:A\to B</math> is said to be '''strong''', if for any [[monomorphism]] <math>\mu:C\to D</math> and for any morphisms <math>\alpha:A\to C</math>  and <math>\beta:B\to D</math> such that <math>\beta\circ\varepsilon=\mu\circ\alpha</math> there exists a morphism <math>\delta:B\to C</math>, such that <math>\delta\circ\varepsilon=\alpha</math> and <math>\mu\circ\delta=\beta</math>. [[File:Diagram-orthogonality-2.jpg|thumb]]</ref>{{sfn|Borceux|1994}}{{sfn|Tsalenko|Shulgeifer|1974}} <math>\beta</math> a [[bimorphism]], and <math>\sigma</math> a [[Monomorphism#Related concepts|strong monomorphism]].<ref>A [[monomorphism]] <math>\mu:C\to D</math> is said to be '''strong''', if for any [[epimorphism]] <math>\varepsilon:A\to B</math> and for any morphisms <math>\alpha:A\to C</math> and <math>\beta:B\to D</math> such that <math>\beta\circ\varepsilon=\mu\circ\alpha</math> there exists a morphism <math>\delta:B\to C</math>, such that <math>\delta\circ\varepsilon=\alpha</math> and <math>\mu\circ\delta=\beta</math></ref>{{sfn|Borceux|1994}}{{sfn|Tsalenko|Shulgeifer|1974}}

== Uniqueness and notations == 
[[File:Uniqueness-of-nodal-decomposition-2.jpg|thumb|Uniqueness of the nodal decomposition.]] If it exists, the nodal decomposition is unique up to an isomorphism in the following sense: for any two  nodal decompositions <math>\varphi=\sigma\circ\beta\circ\pi</math> and <math>\varphi=\sigma'\circ\beta'\circ\pi'</math> there exist [[Morphism#Isomorphisms|isomorphism]]s <math>\eta</math> and <math>\theta</math> such that 
: <math>\pi'=\eta\circ\pi,</math>
: <math>\beta=\theta\circ\beta'\circ\eta,</math>
: <math>\sigma'=\sigma\circ\theta.</math>

[[File:Nodal-decomposition-notations.jpg|thumb|Notations.]] 
This property justifies some special notations for the elements of the nodal decomposition: 
:<math>
\begin{align}
& \pi=\operatorname{coim}_\infty \varphi, && 
P=\operatorname{Coim}_\infty \varphi,\\
& \beta=\operatorname{red}_\infty \varphi, &&  \\
& \sigma=\operatorname{im}_\infty \varphi, &&  
Q=\operatorname{Im}_\infty \varphi,
\end{align}
</math> 
– here <math>\operatorname{coim}_\infty \varphi</math> and <math>\operatorname{Coim}_\infty \varphi</math> are called the ''nodal coimage of <math>\varphi</math>'', <math>\operatorname{im}_\infty \varphi</math> and <math>\operatorname{Im}_\infty \varphi</math> the ''nodal image of <math>\varphi</math>'', and <math>\operatorname{red}_\infty \varphi</math> the ''nodal reduced part of <math>\varphi</math>''.

In these notations the nodal decomposition takes the form
:<math>\varphi=\operatorname{im}_\infty \varphi\circ\operatorname{red}_\infty \varphi \circ \operatorname{coim}_\infty \varphi.</math>

== Connection with the basic decomposition in pre-abelian categories == 
In a [[pre-abelian category]] <math>{\mathcal K}</math> each morphism <math>\varphi</math> has a standard decomposition 
: <math>\varphi=\operatorname{im} \varphi\circ\operatorname{red} \varphi\circ\operatorname{coim} \varphi</math>,
called the ''basic decomposition'' (here <math>\operatorname{im} \varphi=\ker(\operatorname{coker} \varphi)</math>, <math>\operatorname{coim} \varphi=\operatorname{coker}(\ker\varphi)</math>, and <math>\operatorname{red} \varphi</math> are respectively the image, the coimage and the reduced part of the morphism <math>\varphi</math>).

[[File:Nodal-and-basic-decomposition-1.jpg|thumb|Nodal and basic decompositions.]] If a morphism <math>\varphi</math> in a [[pre-abelian category]] <math>{\mathcal K}</math> has a nodal decomposition, then there exist morphisms <math>\eta</math> and <math>\theta</math> which (being not necessarily isomorphisms) connect the nodal decomposition with the basic decomposition by the following identities:
: <math>\operatorname{coim}_\infty \varphi=\eta\circ\operatorname{coim} \varphi,</math>
: <math>\operatorname{red} \varphi=\theta\circ\operatorname{red}_\infty \varphi\circ\eta,</math>
: <math>\operatorname{im}_\infty \varphi=\operatorname{im} \varphi\circ\theta.</math>

== Categories with nodal decomposition == 
A category <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is called a ''category with nodal decomposition''{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=28}} if each morphism <math>\varphi</math> has a nodal decomposition in <math>{\mathcal K}</math>. This property plays an important role in constructing [[envelope (category theory)|envelope]]s and [[refinement (category theory)|refinement]]s in <math>{\mathcal K}</math>. 

In an [[abelian category]] <math>{\mathcal K}</math> the basic decomposition
: <math>\varphi=\operatorname{im} \varphi\circ\operatorname{red} \varphi\circ\operatorname{coim} \varphi</math>
is always nodal. As a corollary, ''all abelian categories have nodal decomposition''. 

''If a [[pre-abelian category]] <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is linearly complete,<ref name=linearly-complete> A category <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is said to be ''linearly complete'', if any functor from a linearly ordered set into <math>{\mathcal K}</math> has [[direct limit|direct]] and [[inverse limit]]s.</ref> well-powered in strong monomorphisms<ref name=well-powered-in-strong-monomorphisms>A category <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is said to be ''well-powered in strong monomorphisms'', if for each object <math>X</math> the category <math>\operatorname{SMono}(X)</math> of all [[strong monomorphism]]s into <math>X</math> is skeletally small (i.e. has a skeleton which is a set).</ref> and co-well-powered in strong epimorphisms,<ref name=co-well-powered-in-strong-epimorphisms>A category <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is said to be ''co-well-powered in strong epimorphisms'', if for each object <math>X</math> the category <math>\operatorname{SEpi}(X)</math> of all [[strong epimorphism]]s from <math>X</math> is skeletally small (i.e. has a skeleton which is a set).</ref> then  <math>{\mathcal K}</math> has nodal decomposition.{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=37}}''

More generally, ''suppose a category <math>{\mathcal K}</math> is linearly complete,<ref name=linearly-complete /> well-powered in strong monomorphisms,<ref name=well-powered-in-strong-monomorphisms /> co-well-powered in strong epimorphisms,<ref name=co-well-powered-in-strong-epimorphisms /> and in addition strong epimorphisms discern monomorphisms<ref name=strong-epimorphisms-discern-monomorphisms>It is said that ''strong epimorphisms discern monomorphisms'' in a category <math>{\mathcal K}</math>, if each morphism <math>\mu</math>, which is not a monomorphism, can be represented as a composition <math>\mu=\mu'\circ\varepsilon</math>, where <math>\varepsilon</math>  is a [[strong epimorphism]] which is not an isomorphism.</ref> in <math>{\mathcal K}</math>, and, dually, strong monomorphisms discern epimorphisms<ref name=strong-monomorphisms-discern-epimorphisms>It is said that ''strong monomorphisms discern epimorphisms'' in a category <math>{\mathcal K}</math>, if each morphism <math>\varepsilon</math>, which is not an epimorphism, can be represented as a composition <math>\varepsilon=\mu\circ\varepsilon'</math>, where <math>\mu</math>  is a [[strong monomorphism]] which is not an isomorphism.</ref> in <math>{\mathcal K}</math>, then  <math>{\mathcal K}</math> has nodal decomposition.{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=31}}''

The category '''Ste''' of [[stereotype space]]s (being non-abelian) has nodal decomposition,{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=142}} as well as the (non-[[additive category|additive]]) category '''SteAlg''' of [[stereotype algebra]]s .{{sfn|Akbarov|2016|p=164}}
